title: Cannabis Jam Recipe: Easy Infused Raspberry Jam
metaDescription: A small-batch raspberry freezer jam infused after cooking with canna-coconut oil or a tincture, with per-tablespoon dosing and fridge or freezer storage.
excerpt: A bright raspberry jam that doubles as an easy-to-portion edible: the infusion goes in after cooking, so the math per tablespoon stays simple.
keyTakeaways: Cook the jam to its gel point first, then stir in the infusion after about 5 minutes off the heat.
Total mg in the infusion divided by the tablespoons of jam gives the dose per spoonful.
Glycerin and alcohol tinctures mix in easily; coconut oil firms up when chilled and can show as flecks.
Keep it in the fridge or freezer, never the pantry, and label every jar.
body:
This cannabis jam recipe makes a small batch of raspberry freezer jam and stirs the infusion in only after cooking. That spares it the hard boil, and measuring the finished jam first keeps the dose per tablespoon simple.

## Dosing: total mg divided by tablespoons

Divide the THC in your infusion by the tablespoons of finished jam. This batch makes about 2 1/2 cups, or 40 tablespoons, so 100 mg gives roughly 2.5 mg per level tablespoon; half of a tincture labeled 200 mg per bottle would do it. Stir it in for a full minute, then count one level tablespoon as a serving and give it at least 2 hours; our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) explains the wait.

## What you need

Raspberries, fresh or thawed frozen, sugar warmed in a low oven so it dissolves fast, and lemon juice. For the infusion, use a glycerin or alcohol tincture or melted canna-coconut oil. Selection varies by store, so check [your local High Society store's menu](/shop/) for tinctures.

## The cannabis jam recipe, step by step

Bring the berries to a boil, mashing as they soften, then add the warm sugar and lemon juice and boil hard, stirring often. Start testing after about 5 minutes. The jam is ready at 220°F at sea level, minus 2°F per 1,000 feet of elevation. Or spoon a little onto a cold plate and set it in the freezer for a few minutes; if it gels, the jam is ready. Let it cool off the heat for 5 minutes, then stir in the infusion.

## Choosing an infusion

THC dissolves in alcohol, glycerin and fats, so each one carries it into a jam that's mostly fruit, sugar and water.

| Infusion | Taste | Texture |
|---|---|---|
| Glycerin tincture | Sweet, mild | Mixes in easily |
| Alcohol tincture | Sharper, a little boozy | Mixes in easily |
| Canna-coconut oil | Mild | Firms up and can fleck when cold |

See our [tincture guide](/blog/cannabis-tincture-guide/) and [canna oil recipe](/blog/canna-oil-recipe/) for each base.

## Storage and labeling

This isn't a canning recipe, so keep the jam in the fridge or freezer. Ohio State University Extension gives uncooked freezer jams up to three weeks refrigerated or a year frozen, and an opened jar a few days. If you used infused oil, freeze every jar but the open one. Mark each lid "infused," with the mg per tablespoon and the date, and keep the jars apart from your regular jam, out of reach of curious kids and pets.

faq.q: Why add the cannabis after cooking?
faq.a: The jam boils hard to reach its gel point, and your infusion doesn't need that heat. Stirring it in after a few minutes off the burner spares it the boil, and measuring the finished jam first makes the dose per tablespoon easy to work out.

faq.q: How much THC is in a spoonful?
faq.a: Only your own numbers can say. Divide the total mg you stirred in by the tablespoons of finished jam: 100 mg through about 40 tablespoons gives roughly 2.5 mg per level tablespoon. Mix well before filling jars, then try a single level tablespoon and give it at least 2 hours.

faq.q: Can infused jam be canned for the pantry?
faq.a: No. This is a freezer jam, not a tested canning recipe, so it belongs in the fridge or freezer. A pantry shelf is also where an infused jar is most likely to be mistaken for regular jam. Freeze the extras and thaw one jar at a time.

sources.label: National Center for Home Food Preservation (University of Georgia): Making Jam without Added Pectin
National Center for Home Food Preservation (University of Georgia): Testing Jelly without Added Pectin
Ohio State University Extension, Fact Sheet HYG-5348: Preserving Uncooked Jams and Jellies
Public Health Agency of Canada: Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health statement on cannabis extracts, edibles and topicals (2020)

ingredients: 4 cups raspberries, fresh or thawed frozen
Your measured infusion: an alcohol or glycerin tincture, or melted canna-coconut oil (see the note)
steps: Heat the oven to 250°F and warm the sugar in a baking dish for 10 minutes. Put a small plate in the freezer.
Bring the raspberries to a boil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat, mashing as they soften.
Stir in the warm sugar and lemon juice until dissolved, then boil hard, stirring often.
After about 5 minutes, start testing: the jam is ready at 220°F at sea level (2°F lower per 1,000 feet), or when a spoonful on the cold plate gels after a few minutes in the freezer.
Take the pot off the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes. Stir in the measured infusion for a full minute.
Ladle into clean jars, leaving 1/2 inch of headspace, and let them cool. Label every jar, refrigerate one and freeze the rest.
recipe.dosingNote: Estimate only: 100 mg of THC stirred into about 40 tablespoons of jam is roughly 2.5 mg per level tablespoon. With a tincture, go by the label's THC total; homemade oil usually lands below its estimate, depending on the flower and on what decarbing and infusing took out. At that strength, one level tablespoon is a sensible first serving; wait at least 2 hours before having more. Mark every jar and keep them on the top shelf, behind anything kids reach for and away from pets.

claims.claim: The batch makes about 2 1/2 cups, or 40 tablespoons
claims.source: Arithmetic (2.5 x 16 = 40); a kitchen estimate for 4 cups raspberries and 2 cups sugar cooked to the gel point. The text tells readers to measure the finished jam.

claims.claim: 100 mg over 40 tablespoons is about 2.5 mg per level tablespoon; half of a 200 mg tincture supplies 100 mg
One level tablespoon (about 2.5 mg) is a sensible first serving
claims.source: CCMOH statement, Public Health Agency of Canada (Jan. 6, 2020): 'Start with small amounts - 2.5 mg of THC or less for products that you eat or drink.' Opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Give a spoonful 2 hours / wait 2 hours to judge it (body, FAQ, dosing note)
claims.fix: Now 'at least 2 hours' in all three places: full effects can take up to 4 hours.
claims.source: CCMOH 2020: 'It may take up to 2 hours to feel the effects of edible cannabis, and up to 4 hours to feel the full effects.'

claims.claim: Jam is ready at 220 F at sea level, minus 2 F per 1,000 feet of elevation
claims.fix: Recipe step now carries the elevation note too; NCHFP jam page added as the source.
claims.source: NCHFP, Making Jam without Added Pectin (Table 3: sea level 220 F, 1,000 ft 218 F, 2,000 ft 216 F ...); NCHFP, Testing Jelly without Added Pectin: 'For each 1000 feet of elevation above sea level, subtract 2 degrees F.' Both opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Jam is also ready when it slides off a cold (freezer-chilled) metal spoon in a sheet (body, steps 1 and 4)
claims.fix: NCHFP's jam page gives only the refrigerator test (boiling jam on a cold plate, a few minutes in the freezer, ready if it gels); the sheet test is its jelly test and uses a cool, not frozen, spoon. Replaced with the cold-plate test in the body and steps.
claims.source: NCHFP jam page: 'Pour a small amount of boiling jam on a cold plate ... If the mixture gels, it is ready to fill.' NCHFP jelly page: 'Dip a cool metal spoon into the boiling jelly mixture'.

claims.claim: THC dissolves in alcohol, glycerin and fats
claims.source: PubChem CID 16078 (Solubility): '1 part in 1 part of alcohol ... 1 part in 3 parts of glycerol ... Soluble in fixed oils.' Read 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Glycerin and alcohol tinctures 'blend in clear'; coconut oil can look cloudy and fleck when cold (takeaway and table)
claims.fix: No source for clarity in a water-based jam (THC-bearing resin can cloud when an alcohol tincture meets water). Now: tinctures 'mix in easily'; coconut oil 'firms up and can fleck when cold'.
claims.source: PubChem (THC essentially insoluble in water); coconut oil is solid at fridge temperature: Food Chemistry: X (2026), PMC13277645, full text via Europe PMC read 2026-10-24, measured melting points of 25.25 C (77 F) for virgin and 26.86 C (80 F) for refined coconut oil.

claims.claim: Taste: glycerin tincture sweet and mild, alcohol tincture sharper, canna-coconut oil mild
claims.source: Sensory description (glycerin is sweet); not a regulated claim.

claims.claim: This isn't a canning recipe; keep it in the fridge or freezer, not the pantry
claims.source: OSU HYG-5348: unprocessed jams must be refrigerated or frozen; the recipe has no tested processing step.

claims.claim: Ohio State Extension: uncooked freezer jams keep up to three weeks refrigerated or a year frozen; an opened jar a few days
claims.source: OSU HYG-5348 (Treva Williams, rev. May 28, 2015): 'up to three weeks in the refrigerator or for up to a year in the freezer'; use within a few days once opened. Opened 2026-10-24. Applied to this cooked, unprocessed jam as the cautious figure.

claims.claim: Leave 1/2 inch of headspace in freezer jars
If infused oil was used, freeze every jar except the open one
claims.source: Cautious reading of the CDC 4-day limit for homemade oils made with herbs (CDC Botulism Prevention, Feb. 26, 2026).

claims.claim: Method: warm sugar 10 minutes at 250 F, boil and mash berries, boil hard, start testing after about 5 minutes, cool 5 minutes before stirring in the infusion for a full minute
claims.source: Culinary method; adding the infusion off the boil keeps it away from the hottest stage.

claims.claim: Dosing note: 'trust the label' for a tincture
claims.fix: Now 'go by the label's THC total': Michigan labels carry a statement that actual values may vary by 10%.

claims.claim: Dosing note: homemade oil 'lands below its estimate'
claims.fix: Now 'usually lands below'; the outcome depends on the reader's flower and method.
claims.source: Task dosing-note rule; the canna-butter-recipe worksheet gives a ceiling, not a measurement.

claims.claim: High Society: selection varies by store; check your local store's menu for tinctures
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.productCategories (tinctures on the Birch Run and New Buffalo menus); no product or stock is claimed.

review.factCheckNotes: Fact-check 2026-10-24: 17 claims checked, 5 fixed (wait time, doneness test, 'blends in clear', 'trust the label', 'lands below'). Added the NCHFP jam page; all cited URLs opened.
review.writerNotes: Not presented as a canning recipe (mustAvoid). Uncooked-jam storage times from Ohio State are applied to this cooked, unprocessed freezer jam; jars made with infused oil go to the freezer except the open jar, to stay consistent with the CDC 4-day limit for homemade herb oils. Yield of about 2 1/2 cups is a kitchen estimate; readers measure the finished jam. Title changed from the brief's hsTitle so the primary keyword (cannabis jam recipe) leads it.
